action: The presentation introduces proportions, overall head forms, and individual facial features before sculpting.
why: Establish the sequence of the face lesson.

action: The presenter points to the top of a front-view head beside its profile while introducing the eye-height landmark.
why: Relate the eye line to the full height from crown to jaw.

action: The presenter draws a crown-to-chin centerline and a horizontal line halfway down through the eyes.
why: Locate the eye line relative to the complete head, not just the face below the hairline.
reader_equivalent: Use face_landmarks to calculate the crown-to-chin midpoint.

action: The labeled eye line remains superimposed across the front reference at the head-height midpoint.
why: Use this first horizontal landmark to organize subsequent features.
reader_equivalent: Compare the eye line against the midpoint of the head bounds.

action: The slide switches to brow and nose placement and the presenter points near a proposed hairline.
why: Set a hairline starting point before dividing the face into thirds.

action: The presenter brackets the hairline-to-chin distance and draws two horizontal divisions across the face.
why: Place the brow and nose base at the boundaries of the middle third.
reader_equivalent: Calculate thirds between the chosen hairline and chin.

action: The presenter outlines the ear between the marked brow and nose-base levels.
why: Establish a starting vertical range for the ear while allowing character variation.
reader_equivalent: Compare ear top and bottom against the brow and nose-base landmarks.

action: The brow and nose-base guide lines are extended from the front head across the profile.
why: Check the ear and rear head against the same horizontal landmarks in profile.
reader_equivalent: Compare these landmarks in front and side views.

action: The slide changes from ear-height guides to a profile-depth diagram and its explanatory text.
why: Introduce depth relationships between the eye and nose instead of judging only the front silhouette.

action: The presenter marks the eye region on the profile to define the first depth interval.
why: Use the eye's profile depth as a unit for comparing nose projection.

action: The presenter adds equal-unit marks from the eye region toward the nose bridge in the profile drawing.
why: Compare the eye depth interval with the interval to the nose bridge.
reader_equivalent: Compare feature depths in side view rather than assuming a flat face.

action: Three equal profile-depth marks are shown before the slide introduces the nose-to-chin midpoint for lip placement.
why: Transition from eye-to-nose depth to the vertical location of the mouth.
reader_equivalent: Check lip bottom against the midpoint from nose base to chin.

action: The presenter bisects the distance from the nose base to the chin and sketches lips above that midpoint.
why: The midpoint indicates the bottom of the lips, not the mouth opening.
reader_equivalent: Use the midpoint as a lower-lip boundary when placing the mouth.

action: The lip guide is cleared and the presenter introduces the gap between the two eyes.
why: Set a baseline for eye spacing before detailing.
reader_equivalent: Compare the inter-eye gap to one eye width in front view.

action: The presenter marks one eye's width and begins transferring that span into the gap between the eyes.
why: Make the eye spacing comparable to the width of one eye.
reader_equivalent: Measure eye width and inter-eye gap in the same front projection.

action: Three adjacent marked spans run across one eye, the gap, and the other eye.
why: Show the standard spacing as a starting point that stylized designs may alter.
reader_equivalent: Compare the two eye widths and their intervening gap.

action: A mouth-width guideline appears alongside the eye-spacing reference.
why: Keep mouth corners within the eye-midpoint boundaries as a general guide.
reader_equivalent: Compare mouth corners to verticals through the eye centers.

action: The presenter dots the center of an eye and draws a vertical line down beside the mouth.
why: Show the lateral limit for that mouth corner.
reader_equivalent: Project each eye center vertically to check mouth width.

action: The vertical eye-to-mouth guide is removed, leaving the unmarked reference and proportion notes.
why: Conclude the mouth-width comparison before moving to head forms.

action: The presentation shifts from facial proportions to identifying the cranium and jaw as the two main masses.
why: Simplify the head before adding smaller planes.

action: A faceted head diagram appears in three-quarter and front views beside a list of major facial planes.
why: Make the forehead, eye band, temple, face side, and chin plane changes legible.
reader_equivalent: Compare the head sculpt from front and three-quarter views before adding detail.

action: The labeled head-plane diagram gives way to an eye-socket illustration.
view: front plane diagram then eye illustration
why: Relate the large head planes to eyes recessed into sockets rather than pasted onto a flat face.

action: The presenter circles the profile eyeball inside a surrounding socket and then introduces eyelid edges.
why: Emphasize the depth relationship between the eyeball and surrounding face.
reader_equivalent: Check the eyeball's recession within the socket from the side.

action: A colored lid diagram and a side-view eyeball depict eyelids curving around a spherical eye.
why: Distinguish the eye-contact edge, eyelid fold, and transition to the face.
reader_equivalent: Shape eyelid ridges around the eyeball rather than in a flat plane.

action: The presenter traces successive upper-lid edges on the colored eye diagram.
why: Separate the rim touching the eyeball from the fold and outer facial transition.
reader_equivalent: Refine the lid contact, crease and outer transition as distinct features.

action: The presenter marks corresponding upper-lid points on the front diagram and its side cross-section.
view: front eye diagram and side cross-section
why: Connect the visible bands to their positions around the eyeball in depth.
reader_equivalent: Inspect the upper lid from the side as well as the front.

action: Additional marks identify corresponding lower-lid bands on the diagram and cross-section.
view: front eye diagram and side cross-section
why: Apply the same three-dimensional edge interpretation to the lower lid.
reader_equivalent: Inspect lower-lid contact and transition in both views.

action: The nose slide presents a simple rounded triangular block progressing to more detailed noses and multiple reference angles.
why: Establish the large nose mass and compare references before adding anatomy.
reader_equivalent: Block the nose as a simple volume and compare front, side and underside views.

action: The presentation displays successive lip sculpt stages and drawings of curved mouth forms.
why: Treat the lips as a three-dimensional form wrapping the teeth rather than a flat mark.
reader_equivalent: Build the mouth mound before cutting the lip separation.

action: The presenter draws brow-height and nose-base guides across a head in the ear reference sheet.
why: Bracket the ear vertically between those facial landmarks.
reader_equivalent: Compare ear bounds with brow and nose-base levels.

action: The presenter outlines a small triangular wedge at the side of a front-view head.
why: Simplify the ear's overall attachment and silhouette before internal detail.
reader_equivalent: Block the ear as a wedge attached to the side of the head.

action: The presenter traces a question-mark-like outer ear curve next to diagrams showing a branching inner form.
view: ear construction sheet and sculpt references
why: Organize the outer rim and interior ridge into recognizable simple shapes.
reader_equivalent: Use ear references to shape the rim and branching inner ridge after the base wedge.

action: The video transitions into Blender with a faceted full-body blockout, a head close-up, and a face-reference collage visible together.
view: perspective full body with front head reference panel
why: Resume work from the existing character blockout with references in sight.

action: In Sculpt Mode the artist orbits the faceted head and draws an annotation around the cranium in profile.
why: Identify the cranium and jaw masses before reshaping them.
reader_equivalent: Inspect the head from front and side and identify the cranium/jaw break.

action: The head is shown in Sculpt Mode as the artist returns to Grab and rotates toward a three-quarter view.
why: Prepare the head for smoothing after the narrated remesh; the sampled frames do not independently show the remesh operation.
reader_equivalent: Set the head's voxel remesh resolution and smooth the resulting surface.

action: The artist holds Shift to smooth the head, isolates it, zooms in and continues smoothing from an oblique view.
why: Remove coarse facets while preserving the broad cranium and jaw volumes.
reader_equivalent: Use broad low-strength sculpt_strokes smoothing passes across the isolated head.

action: The artist switches from an oblique inspection to front orthographic and positions Crease Polish near the middle of the blank head.
view: isolated front orthographic after oblique view
why: Prepare to mark the eye line after establishing the primary head masses.
reader_equivalent: Compute the eye-line landmark and place a shallow horizontal crease with sculpt_strokes.

action: The artist continues a shallow horizontal eye-line groove around the front toward the side, stopping before the back of the head.
why: Define the eye band in three dimensions without cutting a complete ring around the skull.
reader_equivalent: Use a shallow crease along the front and lateral eye line, stopping short of the rear.

action: With Grab, the artist pulls the eye-line area inward in profile and checks the resulting band from the front.
why: Recess the eye region and leave projection available for the nose.
reader_equivalent: Use broad grab sculpt_strokes to recess the eye band, then inspect from front and side.

action: The artist holds Shift to smooth the area immediately above the recessed eye line while viewing the head from the front.
why: Begin defining the brow shelf by softening the upper edge of the eye band.
reader_equivalent: Apply gentle smoothing strokes above the eye-line groove while retaining the brow plane.

action: Annotate tool: draws guide lines marking thirds (1/3 marks) over the front-ortho head, then switches to Grab (Size 154px, Strength 0.400) and orbits to a perspective view.
why: Check facial thirds against the head before sculpting.

action: Crease Polish with Ctrl held (subtract) drawn as one horizontal line across the brow band; follows with smoothing and a view orbit to check it.
why: Mark the eyebrow line as a groove at the band edge.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes: one crease/subtract stroke across x at brow height, radius ~ 1/10 head width, then smooth pass

action: Scrape/Fill brush used in broad passes on the temple/side of the head to flatten it; size changes repeatedly with F between passes.
why: Clean the side of the head into a flat plane.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes brush=scrape/flatten, radius ~0.4 of head height, 2-3 passes down the temple

action: Crease Polish (Ctrl) re-marks the edge, then Scrape/Fill at 206px marks/flattens the side plane of the face; view orbits between 3/4 and side with Alt-drag.
why: Define the plane break between front and side of the face.
reader_equivalent: scrape stroke along the cheek plane edge from brow to jaw

action: Scrape/Fill at 204px dragged in short strokes down the side of the jaw/cheek to give the face side plane; cursor is an ellipse, so strokes are oblique.
why: Plane out the side of the face down to the jaw.
reader_equivalent: scrape strokes following the jaw line, brow to chin

action: Scrape/Fill finishes, then Crease Polish at 104->80px with Ctrl draws a short curved line at the chin and Shift+C re-selects it; view is looking up at the chin.
view: User Perspective (Local), underview of the chin
why: Mark out the chin underside crease simply.
reader_equivalent: one short subtract arc below the lower lip area

action: Grab at 178->130px, Strength 0.400, nudges the chin and cheek volume; MasterClass reference panel is enlarged then shrunk while comparing; Shift smooths.
why: Compare to reference, then adjust jaw/chin masses.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab at chin/cheek: small displacements ~2-4% of head height

action: Nose is a separate sphere object: Ctrl+Tab enters sculpt, X symmetry is enabled in the header, Grab (130 to 270px) pulls it into the face; X-ray toggled with Alt+Z.
why: Block the nose as a ball and push it into the face before shaping.
reader_equivalent: create sphere via bpy at nose position, scale ~0.25 head width; sculpt_strokes grab to merge it with symmetry on

action: Grab Size 206-296px pulls the nose sphere down into a tapered nose shape, switching between side and front view; Alt+Z X-ray again.
why: Shape a nose with a drooping tip.
reader_equivalent: grab stroke downward at the nose tip, ~radius nose width

action: Draw brush (Ctrl=subtract) at 80px, Strength 0.5 indents the underside of the nose for nostrils; Grab 224/140/270px pushes form; mesh is visibly blocky at this resolution.
why: Give the nose underside/nostril form.
reader_equivalent: draw/subtract strokes at underside; grab sideways

action: Object Mode: selects the nose and head and joins them with Ctrl+J, returns to sculpt, and opens the voxel Remesh overlay (grid over the face, size readout on screen) to unify the mesh.
why: Join the objects and remesh into one even-resolution mesh.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.object.join(); then sculpt_remesh(object=..., voxel_size=...) at the stage file's step 9 value

action: Annotate guide lines over the nose bridge, then Clay Strips (Size 84 then 156px, Strength 0.5) adds volume up toward the brow; Shift smoothing follows.
why: Grow the nose out of the face toward the brow.
reader_equivalent: clay-strip strokes upward from nose bridge to the brow, then smooth

action: Clay Strips 110->96px at 0.5 adds volume on the side of the nose, Shift+smooth passes (F x4), then Crease Polish starts the brow line.
why: Blend the nose flanks into the face.
reader_equivalent: clay strips along nose side + smooth

action: Crease Polish (Ctrl) at 84px, Strength 0.250 draws the brow line across front and 3/4; orbits and zoom out with Alt/Ctrl+Alt between segments.
why: Define the eyebrow line.
reader_equivalent: subtract stroke across the brow, both sides

action: Object mode: new UV Sphere (named Sphere) for an eyeball is moved with G, X, Z; right-click Object menu to Shade Smooth; Q quick-favourites opens.
why: Place an eyeball and smooth its shading.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.mesh.primitive_uv_sphere_add; bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth()

action: In the Modifiers tab, Add Modifier search 'mirr' and right-click to add to quick favourites; Q menu now lists Mirror among Origin to Geometry, Round Cube, Purge, Solidify, Use Simplify, Shrinkwrap, In Front.
why: Add a Mirror modifier to the eyeball and keep it handy.
reader_equivalent: bpy: obj.modifiers.new('Mirror','MIRROR')

action: Mirror modifier added to the eyeball: Axis X, Mirror Object set to the head (Roundcube); S scales the eye and a second eye appears on the mirrored side.
why: Mirror eyeball about the head center.
reader_equivalent: m=obj.modifiers.new('Mirror','MIRROR'); m.use_axis[0]=True; m.mirror_object=head

action: Eyeball scaled and moved (S, Z, G X, G Y) in object mode; reference image checked to see wide spacing between the eyes; moved apart.
why: Space eyes per the reference.
reader_equivalent: obj.location, obj.scale on eyeball; mirror modifier handles the other eye

action: Switches to sculpt mode on the head: Grab Size 170->184px Strength 0.4 pushes the sockets back so eyelids have room; eyeballs remain visible via mirror.
why: Prepare eye sockets.
reader_equivalent: grab stroke back (-Y) at eye position, radius ~ eye width x1.5

action: Grab (Size 142-148px) pushes the socket area back then Shift smooth; compared in front and 3/4 views; reference panel enlarged.
why: Finish eyelid prep and compare to reference.
reader_equivalent: grab then smooth

action: Grab pulls the upper edge of the socket up and the lower part down, Size 144->400->272->184px, resizing with F repeatedly while orbiting.
why: Character-specific eye angle tweak.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes outer corner up and inner lower

action: Grab Size 232px strokes on eye area; viewed from the side by Alt-drag to check where the eyes face; Strength 0.4.
why: Check eye direction and adjust.
reader_equivalent: grab strokes on eyeball area

action: Grab at 440px smooths overall shapes; Shift+Alt orbit; Draw brush (V) 440->76px at Strength 0.500 starts drawing upper eyelids.
why: Add eyelid form with Draw.
reader_equivalent: draw strokes along upper lid arc, brush radius ~ 1/6 eye width

action: Draw brush 94px Strength 0.5 builds upper eyelid; then Grab 300->258px reshapes the eye while comparing the reference image.
why: Shape the upper eyelid.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes draw arc above eye; grab to reshape

action: Draw 100->68px lower lids, Shift smooth, Grab 268px; mesh edges around the eyelid look stair-stepped.
why: Add lower eyelids.
reader_equivalent: draw strokes along lower lid

action: Grab at 244/298/170/302px (F x5-x16) lowers and raises eyelid corners; orbit/zoom to check the full head front view.
why: Fix lid positions to match character.
reader_equivalent: grab small nudges

action: Grab at 98px with smoothing; the reference panel is enlarged (eye close-up, then face photo) to compare the eyes.
why: Compare eyes to the reference.

action: Crease Polish (Shift+C) 64-66px Strength 0.250, Ctrl held draws the eyelid edge along the upper arc; Grab 98px before it.
why: Define the eyelid edge.
reader_equivalent: subtract crease along lid margin

action: Scrape/Fill 148px Strength 0.7 flattens the ring around the eye; Grab 326/226px pulls lids back to wrap around the eyeball.
why: Plane out lids and wrap around the ball.
reader_equivalent: scrape on lid ring; grab lid edge inward

action: Crease Polish 78px Ctrl marks the lid edge; Scrape/Fill 98px 0.7 (Shift+T) flattens the area outside it.
why: Edge then flatten.

action: Grab 98->268px pulls the lid into place (wrap around eyeball), then Crease Polish 68-72px defines the edge transition into the face.
why: Finish eyelid edge.

action: Shift-smooth passes (F x4) with Grab 90/156/120px at Strength 0.400 across the transition between nose and eye corners; orbit to front.
why: Blend eye-nose transition.
reader_equivalent: smooth strokes

action: Side-profile Grab (120/226/168px) pulls the nose tip back to make it smaller; Shift+Alt orbit to side view.
why: Reduce nose projection.
reader_equivalent: grab nose tip toward +Y

action: Grab 350/140/208/192px pulls nose closer from front; Shift smooth; then pulls out the nose wings.
why: Narrow the nose.

action: Crease Polish 54px 0.250 defines nostrils from below; Alt-rotate to underview; Grab 182/144px rounds the nose bottom; Shift smooth.
why: Round the nose underside.

action: Crease Polish 216->92px Strength 0.250 marks the mouth/lip line and the chin below the nose; views front and below.
why: Define the lip line and chin.

action: Grab 230->454->234->312px reshapes the chin from the side and front; Ctrl+Alt orbit.
why: Refine chin shape.

action: Large Grab (about 414 to 464px, Strength 0.4) nudges the lower face while viewing front and side, with the reference panel visible for comparison.
why: Decide what to change by comparing with the reference.

action: Clay Strips (about 108 to 290px, Strength 0.5) adds volume around the mouth/lip mound, then Shift smooth; orbits to check.
why: Add lips and cheek volume.

action: Clay Strips still active at 280px, Numpad 1 to Front Orthographic, then Crease Polish (280 to 76px, Strength 0.25) starts marking the mouth corners.
why: Define mouth corners.

action: Draws a vertical guide from the eye center toward the mouth and chooses a corner inside it.
why: Sets mouth width against the iris center.
reader_equivalent: Use facial landmarks to position symmetric mouth corners.

action: Marks a mouth corner and rotates to profile before switching to a broad Grab brush.
why: Recesses the mouth corners to follow the curved dental volume.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with crease and then grab at the corner.

action: Pulls the mouth region forward with Grab and checks the result from side and front.
why: Gives the mouth forward projection while retaining recessed corners.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with a broad grab on the mouth mound.

action: Cuts a nearly horizontal mouth seam between the corners and checks the head in profile.
why: Establishes a simple initial lip division.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with crease along each half of the mouth.

action: Switches from Crease Polish to a large Grab and pulls the mouth lower.
why: Corrects the mouth height before refining the lips.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab the mouth region downward.

action: Uses a large Grab on the lips in profile, moving the lip mass forward.
why: Adds depth to lips that were too flat.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab the lips forward.

action: Pulls and adjusts the upper lip with Grab while examining it close in profile.
why: Places the upper lip ahead of the lower lip and introduces curvature.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab the upper lip forward with local falloff.

action: Changes from Grab to Inflate/Deflate and works immediately below the mouth seam.
why: Builds the lower-lip volume.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with inflate across the lower lip.

action: Uses a large Grab over the mouth then zooms out to check the whole face from the front.
why: Lowers the lip region to better match the reference.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab the mouth down, then compare a front capture.

action: Smooths raised cheek and mouth-adjacent areas while the Clay Strips brush remains selected.
why: Blends the freshly built facial volumes into their surroundings.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with smooth across cheek and lip transitions.

action: Smooths the lower lip and chin transition, then uses a broad Grab to adjust the profile.
why: Softens the lip transition and corrects its silhouette.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes smooth followed by grab on the lip profile.

action: Invokes the voxel-size preview and decreases its displayed value from 0.0170 m to 0.0128 m.
why: Prepares finer resolution for detail; the shown value is a preview.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_remesh with voxel size scaled to the head.

action: Uses inverted Draw inside the nostril and then changes to Crease Polish along its rim.
why: Deepens the nostril while clarifying its border.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes subtractive draw in the nostril followed by a small crease on the rim.

action: Adjusts the nose with a large Grab and moves the cursor to the eye region while orbiting.
why: Refines the nose silhouette and checks surrounding proportions.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab on the nose, then inspect front and side captures.

action: Leaves Sculpt Mode for Object Mode and selects the eyeball.
why: Prepares to color the iris separately from the head.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.object.mode_set(mode="OBJECT") and select the eye object.

action: Paints the exposed selected iris faces black in Vertex Paint, then returns to Object Mode.
why: Limits the dark color to the selected iris area.
reader_equivalent: Use bpy mesh color attributes on selected iris faces.

action: Returns to sculpting and follows the lower eyelid and outer corner with Crease Polish.
why: Refines the lid boundary after the iris makes the eye direction visible.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes crease along the lower eyelid and outer corner.

action: Works along the lower eyelid and both corners with a small Crease Polish brush, then zooms out.
why: Checks whether the lid edge reads cleanly around the colored eye.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes crease around the lower lid, then inspect the full face.

action: Smooths the brow region and rotates to the front to adjust the lower jaw with Grab.
why: Softens brow forms and prepares a more pointed jaw silhouette.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes smooth over the brow and grab the jaw.

action: Uses a broad Grab around the cheek and rotates between frontal and three-quarter views.
why: Adjusts cheek fullness and face shape against the reference.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with broad grab on the cheek, inspecting multiple views.

action: Adds Mirror to the eyebrow strip with the head as mirror object, followed by Solidify.
why: Creates a symmetric pair of thicker placeholder brows.
reader_equivalent: bpy modifiers.new for MIRROR and SOLIDIFY, with head as mirror_object.

action: Returns to Object Mode and inspects the mirrored eyebrow strips around the face.
why: Makes the temporary brows read as smooth shapes.
reader_equivalent: bpy.ops.object.shade_smooth() on the eyebrow object.

action: Opens the vertex paint color picker and raises the value above pure black.
why: Keeps the dark eyebrow form legible instead of making it completely black.
reader_equivalent: Assign a dark nonblack color attribute with bpy.

action: Shows the dark eyebrow strips, enters Edit Mode on their object, and enables X-ray.
why: Prepares the existing placeholder geometry for making eyelashes.
reader_equivalent: Use bpy mesh editing to create lash geometry in the brow object.

action: Inspects the dark upper-lash strip, exits local view, and selects the separate ears.
view: front close-up then full upper body
why: Finishes the placeholder eye framing and moves on to the ear objects.
reader_equivalent: Select the ear object with bpy after inspecting the lash silhouette.

action: Uses a broad Grab brush on the separate ear mass from several oblique angles.
why: Positions and reshapes the ear relative to the reference.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_begin on the ear object and use broad grab strokes.

action: Adjusts the ear perimeter and its attachment with a large Grab while orbiting.
why: Rounds the ear mass and checks its placement on the head.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes with broad grab around the ear silhouette.

action: Opens Quick Favorites and selects the Lasso Mask tool before zooming in on the ear.
why: Prepares a region of the ear for a controlled deformation.
reader_equivalent: Create a sculpt mask on the ear via bpy or the available sculpt interface.

action: Undoes a mask that reached the rear, enables Front Faces Only, and lassos the inner ear while leaving a rim.
why: Prevents the mask from selecting the back of the ear.
reader_equivalent: Set the mask only on forward-facing vertices inside the ear-shaped region.

action: Inverts the ear mask and switches to a very broad Grab while viewing the ear from behind.
why: Protects the rim while leaving the inner ear available to move inward.
reader_equivalent: Invert the sculpt mask and grab the unmasked bowl inward.

action: Clears the mask, previews voxel size 0.0149 m, remeshes, and smooths the stepped inner ear.
tool: Clear Mask; Voxel Remesh; temporary Smooth
why: Softens the coarse hollow and rounded rim after the masked deformation.
reader_equivalent: Clear the sculpt mask, sculpt_remesh the ear, then smooth its bowl.

action: Traces the inner perimeter of the ear with Crease Polish, including the lower front fold.
why: Separates the rolled rim from the recessed bowl.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes crease along the inner helix and lower fold.

action: Alternates Grab and Crease Polish around the small lower-front projection inside the ear.
why: Adjusts the protrusion and redefines its border.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes grab the projection and crease its boundary.

action: Sketches a Y in annotation and adds raised branching strokes inside the ear with Clay Strips.
why: Introduces simplified internal ear cartilage.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes clay_strips along two branching inner-ear paths.

action: Adds material to the inner ear branches, smooths them, and sharpens the resulting folds with Crease Polish.
tool: Clay Strips; temporary Smooth; Crease Polish
why: Turns rough branching buildup into softer, separated anatomical folds.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes clay_strips, smooth, and crease along the branch boundaries.

action: Refines the ear fold and adjusts the voxel preview from 0.00922 m to 0.00867 m.
why: Prepares a finer remesh for the ear details; the displayed number is a preview.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_remesh the ear with a finer voxel size relative to its dimensions.

action: Remeshes and smooths the ear, then follows the inner folds with Crease Polish.
tool: Voxel Remesh; temporary Smooth; Crease Polish
why: Retains the large ear forms while softening remesh artifacts and sharpening the folds.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_remesh, then sculpt_strokes smooth and crease on the ear.

action: Works along several inner-ear boundaries with a small Crease Polish brush.
why: Clarifies the rim and branching cartilage without adding separate geometry.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes crease along the inner ear and lower fold.

action: Zooms out from the ear to the full character and rotates to profile while checking the face.
why: Checks how the completed face and separate ear read in the whole character.
reader_equivalent: Capture front and side views and compare the facial silhouette.

action: Shows a black title card and course logo rather than a sculpting operation.
why: Introduces the following body-sculpting chapter.
